premises: Solid-solution strengthening in fcc 3d CCAs originates from configurational fluctuation of atomic-level pressure.
The atomic-level pressure fluctuation is driven by charge transfer between neighboring elements.
A proportional relationship exists between the ensemble standard deviation of atomic-level pressure (ΔPsolute) and solid-solution strength (σSS).
The Hall-Petch effect is temperature-invariant, so σSS carries the temperature-dependent portion of yield strength.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase fcc CCAs with negligible differences in moduli and Burgers vectors.
